title: Find the margin of error from a given interval
subtitle: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  · 2 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **2 of the official questions in Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 0 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're told the sample mean or percent AND the resulting 'between L and U' range, and the question asks what the margin of error is.
- The choices are single small numbers.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Subtract the sample value from the upper bound (or subtract the lower bound from the sample value).
- 2) Check that the other side gives the same distance.
- If the sample value isn't given, use (U − L)/2.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You give the full width of the interval (U − L) instead of half of it.
Or you give one of the endpoints themselves.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
